title: When and Other Time Clauses
summary: Use when, before, while, after and until to show how events relate in time. Describe future plans with a present form in the time clause.
learningObjectives: Place when-clauses before or after a main clause with appropriate punctuation.
Use when, before, after and while to show the order or overlap of actions.
Use a present-tense verb after when and similar time words for future situations.
Use until to say how long an action will continue.

explanation.heading: When links an event to a time
explanation.body: A when-clause tells us the time at which another event happens or happened. It can come at the beginning or at the end of a sentence. The main idea remains the same if you change the order.
explanation.example: We started dinner when our guests arrived.

explanation.heading: Comma when the time clause comes first
explanation.body: When the sentence begins with a time clause, put a comma after it. Normally no comma is needed when the time clause follows the main clause.
explanation.example: When our guests arrived, we started dinner.

explanation.heading: Before, after, while and until
explanation.body: Before shows an earlier action; after shows a later action; while describes actions that overlap in time. Until marks the time when an activity or situation ends. These time clauses can often appear at the start or end of a sentence.
explanation.example: I read a magazine while my sister prepared lunch.

explanation.heading: Future time clauses use the present
explanation.body: If the main clause refers to the future, use the present simple after when, before, after and until—not will. Use will or be going to in the main clause as needed. A time clause with while can also use a present form for a future situation.
explanation.example: I will check the address before I leave tomorrow.

explanation.heading: Different tenses for past and future
explanation.body: Choose the tense according to the situation. For a finished event in the past, use past forms; for a future time clause, use a present form. Do not put will in the time clause just because the event is in the future.
explanation.example: When the film ended last night, everyone stood up.

left.label: Time clause first
left.example: When the bell rang, the pupils left.
left.note: A comma separates the opening time clause from the main clause.

right.label: Time clause last
right.example: The pupils left when the bell rang.

comparisons.title: Future time: main clause versus time clause

left.label: Future main clause
left.example: I will call you after the appointment.
left.note: Will places the main action in the future.

right.label: Future when-clause
right.example: I will call you when the appointment ends.
right.note: Ends is present simple in the time clause, not will end.

examples.sentence: I put my phone away when the performance began.
examples.note: Both actions happened in the past.

examples.sentence: Before you open the box, read the label.
examples.note: The before-clause comes first and is followed by a comma.

examples.sentence: The lights went out while we were having dinner.
examples.note: While links the power failure to an activity in progress.

examples.sentence: We will visit the market after it opens on Saturday.
examples.note: Opens is present simple even though Saturday is in the future.

examples.sentence: I will wait in the lobby until you return.
examples.note: Until shows when the waiting will end; return is present simple.

commonMistakes.incorrect: I will message you when I will finish work.
commonMistakes.correct: I will message you when I finish work.
commonMistakes.why: Use present simple after when for a future time.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Before you will start the exercise, read the instructions.
commonMistakes.correct: Before you start the exercise, read the instructions.
commonMistakes.why: A future time clause after before normally takes the present form.

commonMistakes.incorrect: I will stay here until the train will arrive.
commonMistakes.correct: I will stay here until the train arrives.
commonMistakes.why: Use present simple after until to describe a future stopping point.

studyTips: Mark each sentence as past or future before selecting the tense of the time clause.
Practise both orders: “When the lesson starts, we will listen” and “We will listen when the lesson starts.”
Check for a comma after a time clause at the beginning, and check for present simple after when or until in future sentences.

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence with the correct future time clause.
choices: I will email you when I arrive.
I will email you when I will arrive.
I will email you when will I arrive.
exercises.feedback: Use present simple arrive after when even though the email will be sent later.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence follows the usual punctuation rule for an opening when-clause?
choices: When the show finished we went for tea.
When the show finished, we went for tea.
When, the show finished we went for tea.
exercises.feedback: A comma normally follows a when-clause at the beginning of a sentence.

exercises.prompt: Which expression introduces an activity that can overlap with another action?
choices: after I washed the dishes
before I washed the dishes
while I was washing the dishes
exercises.feedback: While describes a period during which another event can happen.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct sentence about waiting for a future event.
choices: I will wait until she returns.
I will wait until she will return.
I will wait until will she return.
exercises.feedback: Use returns, not will return, after until in a future time clause.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the present simple form of get: “I will put the groceries away when I ___ home.”
acceptedAnswers: get
exercises.feedback: The future time clause after when uses present simple get.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the present simple form of leave: “Please lock the gate before you ___.”
acceptedAnswers: leave
exercises.feedback: After before, use present simple leave for a future action.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the past form of be: “While she ___ reading, the doorbell rang.”
acceptedAnswers: was
exercises.feedback: Was reading describes an activity in progress when the bell rang.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the present simple form of finish: “After we ___ dinner tomorrow, we will watch a film.”
acceptedAnswers: finish
exercises.feedback: After introduces a future time clause, so use present simple finish.

exercises.prompt: Correct the verb in the when-clause: “When I will finish my shift, I will call you.”
acceptedAnswers: When I finish my shift, I will call you.
exercises.feedback: Use finish, not will finish, after when for a future time.

exercises.prompt: Correct the verb in the before-clause: “Before you will go to bed, turn off the lights.”
acceptedAnswers: Before you go to bed, turn off the lights.
exercises.feedback: Use present simple go after before in this instruction.

exercises.prompt: Correct the verb in the after-clause: “After the guests will arrive, we will serve lunch.”
acceptedAnswers: After the guests arrive, we will serve lunch.
exercises.feedback: Use arrive in the time clause even though the event is in the future.

exercises.prompt: Correct the verb in the until-clause: “I will stay here until you will return.”
acceptedAnswers: I will stay here until you return.
exercises.feedback: Use present simple return after until to describe a future endpoint.

speakingExercises.prompt: Join these sentences into one, beginning with “When”: “The alarm rang. I checked the door.”
acceptedAnswers: When the alarm rang, I checked the door.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use a comma after the opening when-clause.

speakingExercises.prompt: Make a complete sentence using these words and the contracted form I'll: “I / text you / when / I / arrive”.
acceptedAnswers: I'll text you when I arrive.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use I'll in the main clause and present simple arrive after when.

speakingExercises.prompt: Arrange these words as a complete sentence beginning with Before: “before / you / start cooking / wash / your hands”.
acceptedAnswers: Before you start cooking, wash your hands.
speakingExercises.feedback: The before-clause comes first, followed by a comma and the instruction.

speakingExercises.prompt: You plan to collect a parcel at the time the post office opens tomorrow. Begin with “I will collect the parcel” and add a when-clause about the post office opening.
acceptedAnswers: I will collect the parcel when the post office opens.
I’ll collect the parcel when the post office opens.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use will in the main clause, but present simple opens after when for a future event.

speakingExercises.prompt: Move the time clause to the beginning, starting with “After”: “We will cook dinner after Dad comes home.” Keep the meaning and tense unchanged.
acceptedAnswers: After Dad comes home, we will cook dinner.
After Dad comes home, we’ll cook dinner.
speakingExercises.feedback: An opening after-clause is followed by a comma; comes stays in the present simple.

speakingExercises.prompt: You are waiting for Sarah, who is out. Tell a friend that you will stop waiting when Sarah returns. Start “I will wait here” and use until.
acceptedAnswers: I will wait here until Sarah returns.
I’ll wait here until Sarah returns.
speakingExercises.feedback: Until gives the endpoint of the waiting; returns is present simple even though the event is future.

speakingExercises.prompt: Correct the future time clause and say the entire sentence: “I will water the plants before I will go out.”
acceptedAnswers: I will water the plants before I go out.
I’ll water the plants before I go out.
speakingExercises.feedback: After before, use present simple go to refer to a future event; keep will in the main clause.

speakingExercises.prompt: Yesterday, Dan was washing the dishes when the phone rang. Make one sentence beginning “While Dan”, using past continuous for washing and past simple for the phone ringing.
acceptedAnswers: While Dan was washing the dishes, the phone rang.
speakingExercises.feedback: While introduces an activity in progress, and the past simple describes the event that happened during it.

listeningExercises.audioText: When the lesson finished, Sam packed his bag.
listeningExercises.prompt: What did Sam do when the lesson ended?
choices: He opened a window.
He packed his bag.
He made a phone call.
listeningExercises.feedback: The second clause tells us that Sam packed his bag.

listeningExercises.audioText: I will water the plants before I leave for the weekend.
listeningExercises.prompt: When will the speaker water the plants?
choices: After coming home.
While travelling.
Before leaving.
listeningExercises.feedback: Before indicates that watering the plants will happen earlier than leaving.

listeningExercises.audioText: I will take a short walk when the rain stops.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the present-simple verb that follows the words “the rain” in the recording.
acceptedAnswers: stops
listeningExercises.feedback: The verb is stops, a present form used for a future time clause.

listeningExercises.audioText: When the bakery opens at eight, I will buy some fresh bread.
listeningExercises.prompt: What needs to happen before the speaker can make the purchase?
choices: The shop needs to open.
The speaker needs to finish lunch.
The bread needs to cool down.
listeningExercises.feedback: The purchase will happen when the bakery opens, at eight.

listeningExercises.audioText: I fed the cat before I left for work this morning.
choices: The speaker arrived at work.
The speaker gave the cat food.
The speaker came home again.
listeningExercises.feedback: Before tells us that feeding the cat happened earlier than leaving for work.

listeningExercises.audioText: Please keep the door closed until the children finish their lesson.
listeningExercises.prompt: When is it okay to open the door?
choices: While the children are still learning.
Before the lesson begins.
Once the lesson has ended.
listeningExercises.feedback: Until marks the end of the period when the door must remain closed.

listeningExercises.audioText: I was washing the car while my sister cleaned the windows.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the one-word time connector indicating that the activities overlapped.
acceptedAnswers: while
listeningExercises.feedback: While connects two actions that happened during the same period.

listeningExercises.audioText: We will lock the door before the shop closes.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the present-simple verb you hear immediately after “the shop”.
acceptedAnswers: closes
listeningExercises.feedback: Closes is present simple in the future time clause after before.
